quick_ref.Theme: Time Detective Agency — The Garden Mystery
quick_ref.Grammar Focus: Present Simple for Facts (It grows, It needs) vs. Past Simple
quick_ref.Spiral Review: W19–W26: Past Simple, Sequence words, Feelings

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Present Facts vs. Past Actions
content: Problem: Students often confuse present facts with past events when storytelling.

Solution: Introduce the Present Simple specifically for universal, scientific facts (e.g., "A seed needs water"), explicitly contrasting it with the Past Simple used for specific historical actions (e.g., "Yesterday, I planted a seed").

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce plant vocabulary and Present Simple for general facts.
Session 2: Contrast Present Simple facts with Past Simple narratives.
Session 3: Mastery of explaining the plant growth process.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a plant part flashcard. Student states a fact about it (e.g., "The stem grows up.").
S2 pull-out: Ask a contrast question: "What did you do yesterday? What does a plant do every day?"
Communicative task (Step 5): Information Gap. Student A has half the facts about a sunflower, Student B has the other half. They ask questions to complete the growth chart.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The Garden Mystery: How Plants Grow Detective Luna is investigating the garden! "How do plants grow?" she asks. The gardener explains: "First, you plant a seed in the soil. The seed is small and brown. Then, you water it. Plants need water to grow. Next, the sun shines on the soil. Plants need sunlight too. After that, roots grow down into the soil. A small stem grows up! Then, leaves appear on the stem. The plant has green leaves. Finally, a beautiful flower blooms! A plant needs three things: soil, water, and sun. That's the secret!"

content: 📖 The Garden Mystery: How Plants Grow
Detective Luna is investigating the garden!

The seed is small and brown.
Then, you water it. Plants need water to grow.
Next, the sun shines on the soil. Plants need sunlight too.
After that, roots grow down into the soil.
Then, leaves appear on the stem.
A plant needs three things: soil, water, and sun.
T / F: Leaves use the sun to make food.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W27: seed, soil, water, sun, root
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (seed, soil, water, sun, root) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Present Simple for Facts (It grows, It needs) vs. Past Simple
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Present Simple for Facts (It grows, It needs) vs. Past Simple.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Memories — The Garden Mystery"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Memories — The Garden Mystery".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (seed, soil, water, sun, root usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

STEM/CLIL Extension Notes (teacher only):

PART 6: STEM/CLIL CONNECTION The Plant Life Cycle Read this: A life cycle shows how a living thing grows and changes. For a plant, it starts with a seed. When the seed gets water, it germinates (wakes up). Roots push down. A shoot pushes up to become the stem. Leaves grow to catch sunlight. Flowers bloom to make new seeds. Then the cycle starts again! The diagram shows: A circle of arrows. Top: a brown seed in soil. Right: roots growing down. Bottom: a stem with leaves. Left: a fully grown plant with a flower dropping a new seed.
